dedupe_keys.name: supply chain data for iron ore to finished goods in the u s great lakes dependency

description: This dataset maps customer-supplier relationships in the US steel value chain, from the three US iron ore producers (Cleveland-Cliffs, US Steel and ArcelorMittal) through to finished goods makers such as appliance and automobile manufacturers, to study how the chain depends on commodities shipped on the Great Lakes. The DataCite record says relationships, their dollar value and share of supplier revenue were recorded by hand for year-end 2017 from the Bloomberg Terminal supply chain module, with inventory turnover ratios for 2017 and the five-year average from FactSet, collected in September to November 2018; subsidiaries are marked "Sub" and undisclosed foreign sales "Unk". The authors used it for network analysis of financial risk from water dependency and found inventory turnover a good proxy. It was published by Dennis Sugrue at the University of Michigan on 1 May 2020 on Deep Blue Data, free under CC BY 4.0, with national coverage of US firms. Caveats: the file formats and sizes are not stated on the pages read (Deep Blue showed a Cloudflare check to this session), and the data are a manual extract of commercial databases for one year. For simulation it gives a firm-level supply network to test how a Great Lakes shipping disruption, such as low water or a lock failure, cascades from iron ore to manufacturers. Related catalogue records include the Global supply chain logistics excavator data, the Energy and Industry Facilities Composite and M-FIND.
